P1_pytorch_wilson_loop_gauge_invariant.description: Pytorch: Wilson loop values unchanged after gauge transform A→A+d_alpha on 4x4 lattice

P2_pytorch_covariant_derivative_transfor.description: Pytorch: D_mu psi transforms as e^{i*alpha} D_mu psi under gauge transform — covariance verified numerically

P3_sympy_covariant_derivative_symbolic_p.description: Sympy: D_mu psi transforms as e^{i*alpha} D_mu psi under gauge transform — symbolic cancellation of d_mu alpha terms confirmed

P4_clifford_u1_rotor_is_unit.description: Clifford Cl(2,0): U(1) gauge element U*U_inv = 1 (unit rotor); gauge transform is an invertible rotation

P5_clifford_grade1_transforms_covariantl.description: Clifford: U * e1 * U_inv stays grade-1 — covariant derivative (grade-1 operation) preserved under U(1) gauge rotation

P6_rustworkx_wilson_loop_is_u1_element.description: Rustworkx: Wilson loop around plaquette 4-cycle has |W|=1 — it is a U(1) element

P7_xgi_plaquette_hyperedge_wilson_loop.description: XGI: 4-way plaquette hyperedge Wilson loop matches lattice graph calculation — 4-body interaction is gauge-invariant

P8_pytorch_composed_gauge_transforms_pre.description: Pytorch: composing two gauge transforms gives same Wilson loop as no transform — gauge invariance is a group property

N1_z3_unsat_two_wilson_loop_values_same_.description: Z3 UNSAT: same physical field cannot have two different Wilson loop values — gauge invariance makes W unique

N2_pytorch_plain_phase_is_gauge_dependen.description: Negative: plain phase of psi changes under gauge transform — it is NOT a physical observable (gauge-dependent)

N3_pytorch_link_variable_is_gauge_depend.description: Negative: individual link variable A_{xy} changes under gauge transform — only Wilson loops (closed paths) are gauge-invariant

N4_sympy_open_wilson_line_gauge_dependen.description: Sympy: open Wilson line acquires phase under gauge transform — only closed loops (Wilson loops) are gauge-invariant

N5_clifford_non_unit_rotor_not_gauge_ele.description: Negative: non-unit element (scalar 2) squared is 4 ≠ 1 — valid U(1) gauge elements must be unit rotors

N6_rustworkx_open_path_gauge_dependent.description: Negative: open path Wilson line in lattice graph changes under site gauge transform — only closed 4-cycles are gauge-invariant

B1_pytorch_identity_gauge_transform.description: Boundary: alpha=0 gauge transform is identity — all links and Wilson loops unchanged

B2_pytorch_global_gauge_invariant.description: Boundary: constant (global) gauge transform also leaves Wilson loops unchanged — global ⊂ local gauge group

B3_sympy_covariant_derivative_at_zero_ga.description: Boundary sympy: D_mu psi at A_mu=0 equals ordinary partial derivative — no gauge field = free field

B4_clifford_u1_identity_at_alpha_zero.description: Boundary Clifford: U(1) element at alpha=0 is scalar 1 — identity of the gauge group

B5_z3_sat_gauge_invariant_observable_con.description: Boundary z3 SAT: gauge-invariant observable W_physical=0.6 is consistent with any gauge choice — multiple gauges are equivalent

B6_xgi_trivial_plaquette_wilson_loop_uni.description: Boundary XGI: trivial plaquette (all A=0) has Wilson loop W=1 — vacuum gauge field has unit holonomy

B7_rustworkx_large_wilson_loop_still_u1.description: Boundary: Wilson loop around 8-site plaquette is still |W|=1 — U(1) property holds for any size closed loop
